first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent prior memories (86, 31) converge on simplifying onboarding as a durable lever for both completion and activation—addressing two of the three current problems simultaneously. I verify these two since they most directly justify the chosen action and because 'durable lift' claims are high-value to confirm before committing scarce experiment capacity. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but matching aggressive entry pricing risks a race-to-bottom that erodes long-term qualified revenue and mainly attracts price-sensitive, lower-quality accounts—this is flagged as a downstream risk worth monitoring even though not chosen this week. Referral and enterprise-sales paths are less relevant to this week's acute problems (activation/onboarding decline) and are better suited to future slots. Given single-experiment capacity, I favor a standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout, preserving the ability to reassess based on results and not treating inherited memories as guaranteeing outcomes under today's competitive conditions.

final.rationale: Verified source records confirm both memories with real magnitudes: exp_86 shows completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and retention +3% (durable positive signal); exp_31 shows signup +15%, activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, but a slight -1% retention dip and an explicit note that it has not been replicated outside SMB. Together these directly target this week's two measurable problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) with confirmed, not merely inherited, evidence. I still choose standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because exp_31's non-replication outside SMB and its retention dip warrant continued measurement before scaling further, and because the competitor pricing shock introduces a confound (some of the SMB activation drop may be price-driven, not onboarding-friction-driven) that this experiment won't resolve — flagging that as a downstream revenue risk to monitor rather than assuming onboarding fixes will fully counter competitive share loss. Promotional pricing was not chosen this week despite competitive pressure, since matching aggressive entry pricing risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts and eroding sustainable qualified revenue, the stated primary objective; that option remains available for a future slot with its own verification. Uncertainty is preserved: this is a confirmed but segment-limited signal, not a guarantee, so scale is kept guarded rather than maximal.
